correctness.rationale: The coefficient vector of the fourth argument is exactly the two scalar q equations and the row determinants in the frozen proof. The first-two-row rank-one cone R has codimension 2 and projective degree 3. On its rank-one locus the remaining scalar equation is the irreducible F: the linear coefficient in gamma_(3,1) is primitive and irreducible, and the exhibited evaluation shows it does not divide the constant term. Removing the scaling parameter gives dimension 3n-3. With independent first rows all lower rows lie in their span and one nonzero additional equation forces codimension at least n-1>=4; with both first rows zero the codimension is 6. For the scheme multiplicity, on the alpha_1!=0 chart eliminate beta_1 by writing beta=(beta_1/alpha_1)alpha+u with u_1=0. The row determinants are linear in u_2,u_3 and two of them eliminate both exactly wherever alpha,gamma_3,gamma_4 are independent. This occurs on the rank-one divisor at alpha=e_1, beta=0, gamma_3=e_2, gamma_4=e_3, all later rows zero, with F=0. There the scalar equations reduce to one reduced divisor equation; hence generic multiplicity is one on the unique top component. The cubic alpha·q cuts R with cycle degree 9 and its only divisors are the top component and the hyperplane-row-zero linear space, each with multiplicity one (sF on the rank-one charts). Subtracting the linear component gives degree 8. The cited exact PR=4 remains eventual, not asserted at n=5.
residual_risks: Only the top component and its generic multiplicity are classified; no assertion about smaller components or the full scheme is inferred.
